title: Introduction to WHOIS
shortDescription: Learn what WHOIS is and why it is important.
content: WHOIS is a protocol and database that provides registration information about domain names. Cybersecurity professionals use WHOIS to identify domain ownership, registrar information, creation dates, expiration dates and contact information when available.
example: Run 'whois example.com' to retrieve registration information.

title: Installing WHOIS
shortDescription: Learn how to install WHOIS on different operating systems.
content: WHOIS is preinstalled on many Linux distributions. Windows users can install WHOIS clients or use online services. macOS users can install it using Homebrew if necessary.

title: Running WHOIS Commands
content: The basic syntax is 'whois domain.com'. The output includes registrar details, registration dates, DNS servers and other registration information.

title: Understanding WHOIS Output
content: WHOIS output contains registrar information, creation date, expiration date, updated date, domain status and name servers. Each field helps investigators gather intelligence about the target domain.
example: Identify the registrar of github.com using WHOIS.

title: WHOIS Best Practices
content: Always verify WHOIS results with multiple sources. Respect privacy regulations and remember that WHOIS information may be hidden due to privacy protection services.
example: Compare WHOIS information with DNS Lookup results.
